author: Grace Chen
title: Tokyo Verdy vs Kashima Antlers: Classmethod DAY & Free T-Shirt Giveaway
text:
Tokyo Verdy is preparing for a high-profile clash against the Kashima Antlers on April 29, 2026, marked by a special collaboration known as Classmethod Day. The event, which coincides with the 13th round of the Meiji Yasuda J1 Hyakunen Kouzou League Regional League, aims to merge the excitement of professional football with community engagement through a series of fan giveaways and corporate partnerships.
The match is scheduled to kick off at 13:00 at the Ajinomoto Stadium, a venue that will host thousands of supporters for this holiday-weekend fixture. As part of the festivities, Classmethod Inc., a firm specializing in cloud implementation and AI technology, will serve as the match-day partner, integrating its corporate presence into the stadium’s pre-match and post-match ceremonies.
For fans attending the match, the primary draw is a massive giveaway of original T-shirts. The club has announced that the first 15,000 visitors will receive a commemorative shirt, provided they enter through designated gates. This initiative is designed to create a visual spectacle of solidarity in the stands, though the club has implemented strict distribution rules to ensure a fair process.
Logistics of the T-Shirt Distribution
The distribution of the 15,000 original T-shirts will begin during early entry, which is scheduled for 10:30. To manage the crowd, the club has designated three specific entry points for the giveaway: Main Gate 3, North Gate 2, and Back Gate 2. Supporters are advised that these locations may change without notice depending on weather conditions or stadium requirements.
The inventory is split between adult and children’s sizes to accommodate families. There are 10,000 shirts available for adults and 5,000 for children. The club has emphasized that size assignments are at the discretion of the distribution staff and cannot be requested or exchanged. The shirts will only be handed out at the point of initial entry; once a supporter has passed through the gate, they cannot return to claim a shirt if they missed it during their first passage.
To maintain the integrity of the home-team atmosphere, the club explicitly stated that those wearing away-team merchandise will not be eligible for the giveaway. The club has issued a strict prohibition against the resale of these shirts, regardless of whether the intent is for profit, noting that any such activity will be met with rigorous countermeasures.
Distribution Summary and Constraints
| Category | Quantity | Distribution Point |
|---|---|---|
| Adult Sizes | 10,000 | Main 3, North 2, Back 2 Gates |
| Children’s Sizes | 5,000 | Main 3, North 2, Back 2 Gates |
| Total Available | 15,000 | First-come, first-served from 10:30 |
Corporate Integration and Match Ceremonies
The partnership with Classmethod Inc. extends beyond the merchandise. The company’s leadership will play a visible role in the match-day proceedings. Akira Omori, Executive Officer and General Manager of the Sales Division at Classmethod, is scheduled to deliver a welcome speech to the crowd, setting the tone for the afternoon’s events.
Further integration includes Satoshi Yokota, the Representative Director of Classmethod, who will participate in the referee escort ceremony. This tradition brings corporate partners directly onto the pitch, bridging the gap between the business community and the sporting world. The “Classmethod presents Man of the Match” award will be presented, though this specific honor is contingent upon a Tokyo Verdy victory.
The ‘W-Chance’ Campaign: A Bridge to May 3
The engagement strategy for Classmethod Day does not end with the final whistle on April 29. The club has introduced a “W-Chance Campaign” designed to incentivize fans to attend a second home match on May 3, 2026, against Kashiwa Reysol. This campaign targets a specific subset of the audience: those who received a children’s T-shirt during the Kashima Antlers game.
Fans who wear the kids’ T-shirt from the April 29 match to the May 3 game will be eligible for a second giveaway. A total of 5,000 limited-color versions of the original T-shirt will be distributed. These special editions come in five different color patterns, adding a collectible element to the fan experience. This “double chance” mechanism is a strategic attempt by Tokyo Verdy to maintain momentum and high attendance throughout the holiday period.
While the basic framework of the May 3 campaign has been announced, the club has noted that specific distribution methods and detailed eligibility criteria will be released at a later date via the official Tokyo Verdy website. This phased communication ensures that the focus remains on the immediate challenge of the Kashima Antlers match while building anticipation for the subsequent weekend.
As the date approaches, supporters are encouraged to monitor official club channels for any updates regarding gate changes or weather-related adjustments to the event schedule. The next confirmed checkpoint for fans will be the release of the detailed distribution guidelines for the May 3 Kashiwa Reysol match, expected to follow the conclusion of the April 29 fixture.
We invite readers to share their thoughts on these fan engagement initiatives in the comments below and share this update with fellow supporters.
